text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain ever wake him up at night, and does he complain of pain in his hip or thigh when moving his left leg? I will also examine his hip for limited internal rotation or abduction.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying that the pain is localized to the knee. I am now going to examine his left hip to check for limited internal rotation or abduction, which can refer pain to the knee.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: The patient is in the second grade, lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco or known toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: I have examined his hip and found limited internal rotation and abduction, which suggests the pain is actually originating from the hip rather than the knee.
